origins.section: A Run Is Its Manifest, and the Harness Compares Ten of Them Byte for Byte
Properties Must Hold on Every Drawn Portfolio
A Golden Record Catches a Regression, Not a Rule Error

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-harness-claim: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-harness-claim: The PASS holds for this machine, this OR-Tools (9.15) and this Python; the manifest records all three, so a later run on other versions is compared knowing they changed.
recorded.prompt:q-witness: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-witness: Without it, many drawn portfolios would have no plan, and a property test that skips them tests less than it seems; with it, every one of the 200 cases tests the solver's plan against a plan known to be valid.
recorded.prompt:q-loose-gap: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-loose-gap: The loosened gap returned a plan $584k worse, and nothing else in the suite would have said so: the plan breaks no rule, so a check of it finds nothing, and it repeats ten times out of ten, so the harness passes. Only a record of the reviewed answer catches it.

recorded.prompt:q-harness-claim: Answer ONLY from this question's own text: its stem and its options. Use no knowledge of the subject at all; treat every term as a word you have never met. Pick an option only when the wording itself singles it out: it is longer or more specific than the others, it repeats words from the stem, the others carry absolute terms such as 'always' or 'never', the stem's grammar fits it alone, or it restates the stem. A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. Say which cue decided it, or that none did.
recorded.outcome:q-harness-claim: from the question's text alone, the reader picked none; the key is 'b'
recorded.because:q-harness-claim: b and c both repeat 'the run repeats'. b is the most hedged, but no option uses 'always'/'never', and all four have similar length and specificity. No listed cue decides.
